key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films are the primary nucleation sites for early degradation, and they can now be rapidly detected with imaging plus machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, non-invasive pre-screening tool to flag unstable perovskite films early, supporting more reliable scale-up of tandem solar cell manufacturing.
method: Nano-FTIR to chemically identify impurity phases
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy for rapid defect imaging
Machine learning-supported image analysis for high-throughput impurity quantification
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiates at impurity-perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density exhibited accelerated early degradation.
watch_item: The workflow depends on image quality and chemical validation, so transferability across different film stacks, processing routes, and microscope setups may need recalibration.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
